# Elm Quay gives two buildings one repair log

For eight weeks, the maintenance team at Elm Quay Housing recorded repair reports for two buildings in a shared log from Svale Systems. Here is why the team made the change, how it prepared, what its own trial figures can and cannot show, and how its supervisor judges the result.

By Thomas

Elm Quay Housing manages 640 apartments, and its telephone repair reports and emails used to be stored separately. In September 2025 the company's own maintenance team decided to test a shared repair log in two buildings. The trial has ended, and the team has yet to decide whether to expand it.

## Elm Quay tested the log before choosing Svale

Maya Lind, Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, answered questions about the trial by email. “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done,” Lind wrote. “The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

Before choosing Svale Systems, the team tested whether the log could show the status of each repair. Svale configured the log and trained six staff members in two sessions, while the team kept telephone reporting open for residents.

## Expansion waits on how the categories hold up

Lind also wrote about the preparation: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

The team will decide whether to expand the trial after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.

## The company's own note does not credit the software

An internal trial note from Elm Quay, dated December 4, 2025, says 31 repair reports were entered during the eight-week trial. The note excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period.

The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. The figure covers time to assignment, not to completion. Completion time, cost and resident satisfaction were not measured.

## Lind weighs the trial as a whole

Lind's overall assessment is not drawn from those figures. “I would choose to do the trial again,” Lind wrote. “Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company.

## A checklist comes before any trial of your own

Operations managers weighing a similar trial can read the [implementation checklist](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist) before setting aside their own preparation time. It is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.

# Elm Quay gives two buildings one repair log

For eight weeks, the maintenance team at Elm Quay Housing recorded repair reports for two buildings in a shared log from Svale Systems. Here is why the team made the change, how it prepared, what its own trial figures can and cannot show, and how its supervisor judges the result.

By Thomas

Elm Quay Housing manages 640 apartments, and its telephone repair reports and emails used to be stored separately. In September 2025 the company's own maintenance team decided to test a shared repair log in two buildings. The trial has ended, and the team has yet to decide whether to expand it.

## Elm Quay tested the log before choosing Svale

Maya Lind, Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, answered questions about the trial by email. “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done,” Lind wrote. “The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

Before choosing Svale Systems, the team tested whether the log could show the status of each repair. Svale configured the log and trained six staff members in two sessions, while the team kept telephone reporting open for residents.

## Expansion waits on how the categories hold up

Lind also wrote about the preparation: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

The team will decide whether to expand the trial after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.

## The company's own note does not credit the software

An internal trial note from Elm Quay, dated December 4, 2025, says 31 repair reports were entered during the eight-week trial. The note excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period.

The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. The figure covers time to assignment, not to completion. Completion time, cost and resident satisfaction were not measured.

## Lind weighs the trial as a whole

Lind's overall assessment is not drawn from those figures. “I would choose to do the trial again,” Lind wrote. “Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company.

## A checklist comes before any trial of your own

Operations managers weighing a similar trial can read the [implementation checklist](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist) before setting aside their own preparation time. It is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.

# Elm Quay gives two buildings one repair log

For eight weeks, the maintenance team at Elm Quay Housing recorded repair reports for two buildings in a shared log from Svale Systems. Here is why the team made the change, how it prepared, what its own trial figures can and cannot show, and how its supervisor judges the result.

By Thomas

Elm Quay Housing manages 640 apartments, and its telephone repair reports and emails used to be stored separately. In September 2025 the company's own maintenance team decided to test a shared repair log in two buildings. The trial has ended, and the team has yet to decide whether to expand it.

## Elm Quay tested the log before choosing Svale

Maya Lind, Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, answered questions about the trial by email. “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done,” Lind wrote. “The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

Before choosing Svale Systems, the team tested whether the log could show the status of each repair. Svale configured the log and trained six staff members in two sessions, while the team kept telephone reporting open for residents.

## Expansion waits on how the categories hold up

Lind also wrote about the preparation: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

The team will decide whether to expand the trial after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.

## The company's own note does not credit the software

An internal trial note from Elm Quay, dated December 4, 2025, says 31 repair reports were entered during the eight-week trial. The note excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period.

The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. The figure covers time to assignment, not to completion. Completion time, cost and resident satisfaction were not measured.

## Lind weighs the trial as a whole

Lind's overall assessment is not drawn from those figures. “I would choose to do the trial again,” Lind wrote. “Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company.

# Source-support report: "Elm Quay gives two buildings one repair log"

Draft: scratch/write-run.NkEBNV/draft.md
Source: work/source.md (brief and material, English)
Draft language: en_US. There is no translation, so there are no translation findings. All three quotations are verbatim.

## 1. Claim accounting

| # | Draft passage | Source passage | Difference / verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| T | Title: "Elm Quay gives two buildings one repair log" | "decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; "The trial lasted eight weeks."; "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking…" | **Finding F1.** The title leaves out "trial", and its present tense "gives" states a provision with no time limit. See below. |
| S1 | "A housing company's maintenance team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same repair information." | "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information." (The team is "its own maintenance team". The information is the telephone reports and emails stored in the repair log.) | Supported. "Repair" names the information the context establishes. |
| S2 | "how Elm Quay Housing tested a shared log from Svale Systems" | "decided to trial a shared repair log"; "It chose Svale Systems after testing…" | Supported. |
| S3 | "what its own trial figures can and cannot show" | "Elm Quay's internal trial note…"; "explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software"; "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements." | Supported. |
| S4 | "how its maintenance supervisor judges the result" | "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"; "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." | Supported. |
| B | "By Thomas" | (from the invocation) | Not a finding, as instructed. |
| 1a | "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 apartments" | "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats." | Supported. "Apartments" is the en_US term for the same thing. |
| 1b | "its telephone repair reports and emails used to be stored separately" | "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately." | Supported. The time ("used to be" = "previously") and the scope (unrestricted in both) match. |
| 1c | "In September 2025 the company's own maintenance team decided to test a shared repair log in two buildings." | "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings." | Supported. |
| 1d | "The trial has ended" | "The trial lasted eight weeks." (past tense, completed duration); the note is dated 4 December 2025 | Supported. |
| 1e | "the team has yet to decide whether to expand it" | "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | Supported. |
| H1 | "Elm Quay tested the log before choosing Svale" | "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair." | Supported. The heading claims no comparison with another supplier ("No comparison with another supplier is available"). |
| 2a | "Maya Lind, Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, answered questions about the trial by email." | "Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"; "All interviews occurred by email" | Supported. The customer is Elm Quay, and the quotations concern the trial. |
| 2b | Quotation 1 plus "Lind wrote" | Quotation 1, word for word; the interviews were by email | Verbatim. "Wrote" is supported. |
| 2c | "Before choosing Svale Systems, the team tested whether the log could show the status of each repair." | "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair." | Supported. |
| 2d | "Svale configured the log and trained six staff members in two sessions, while the team kept telephone reporting open for residents." | "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions." "The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents." | Supported. "While" only connects two things the source reports for the same trial. The draft says nothing more about whose staff they were than the source does. |
| H2 | "Expansion waits on how the categories hold up" | "the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs" | Borderline, not reported. The heading leaves out "for larger repairs", but the next body sentence restores it exactly. "Hold up" is vague and states no scope that the body contradicts. Defensible as a compressed heading. |
| 3a | "Lind also wrote about the preparation:" plus quotation 2 | Quotation 2, word for word | Verbatim. The framing "the preparation" is supported by the quotation itself and by Lind's "extra week for preparation". |
| 3b | "The team will decide whether to expand the trial after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | Same wording in the source | Supported. |
| H3 | "The company's own note does not credit the software" | "the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software" | **Finding F2.** The scope is widened from the time difference to the software in general. |
| 4a | "An internal trial note from Elm Quay, dated December 4, 2025, says 31 repair reports were entered during the eight-week trial." | "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered." | 4b | "The note excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial." | "It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial." (The antecedent of "It" is the note.) | Supported. |
| 4c | "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period." | Same wording in the source | Supported. It measures assignment, not completion. |
| 4d | "The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." | "The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." | Supported. |
| 4e | "The figure covers time to assignment, not to completion." | "Median time from report to assignment…"; brief: "Do not turn assignment time into completion time." | Supported. |
| 4f | "Completion time, cost and resident satisfaction were not measured." | "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements." | Supported. The source states that the measurements do not exist ("There are no"), unlike its "No comparison … is available". The draft's "were not measured" keeps that certainty. |
| H4 | "Lind weighs the trial as a whole" | "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." Quotation 3: "I would choose to do the trial again…" | Supported. Choosing to repeat the trial is a judgment on the trial as a whole. The reservation is carried inside the quotation. |
| 5a | "Lind's overall assessment is not drawn from those figures." | "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures." | Supported. | 5b | Quotation 3, split by "Lind wrote" | Quotation 3, word for word | Verbatim. The hedge "but…" is kept. |
| 5c | "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company." | Same wording in the source | Supported. The reservation survives. |
| H5 | "Other teams can begin with a checklist" | Brief: "The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist…" | Supported as the publisher's suggested next step. |
| 6a | "Elm Quay has not yet made its decision on expansion." | "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after…" | Supported. |
| 6b | "Operations managers weighing a similar trial can read the implementation checklist before setting aside their own preparation time." | Brief: audience is operations managers; "implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist" | Supported. This is the author's advice, and the link text describes its destination accurately. |
| 6c | "It is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial." | "it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial" | Supported. |

### Pronoun accounting (person, number, natural gender)

- "its" (S3, S4, 1b, 6a) and "its own" (S3): third person singular, no natural gender. The referent is Elm Quay Housing, a company. Supported.
- "it" in "whether to expand it" (1e): third person singular, no natural gender. The referent is the trial. Supported.
- "It" in "It is a document…" (6c): third person singular, no natural gender. The referent is the checklist. Supported.
- "their own" (6b): third person plural, no natural gender. The referent is operations managers. Supported.
- "We", "us" and "ours" in the quotations: first person plural, the speaker's team. "I": first person singular, Lind. All verbatim from the source.
- Lind: the draft uses no third-person pronoun for Lind (only "Lind" and "Lind's"), so it asserts no natural gender. The source gives none. Correct.
- The draft contains no grammatical-gender issues, since English has no grammatical gender here.

## 2. Findings (source support)

### F1. The title drops "trial" and presents the log as provided without a time limit
- Draft: "Elm Quay gives two buildings one repair log"
- Source: "decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; "The trial lasted eight weeks."; "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
- Difference: the scope and time of the claim change. The source reports an eight-week trial that has ended, with continuation undecided. The title's "gives", with no "trial", reads as an adoption.
- Concrete case: the eight-week trial ended and the two buildings went back to separate telephone and email records while the team checks how the categories work for larger repairs. The source is consistent with this. The title would then be false, while every source statement still holds. No supplied statement says the log stayed in use after the trial.
- Smallest repair: "Elm Quay trials one repair log in two buildings". An alternative is "Elm Quay tests one repair log in two buildings".

### F2. The heading widens "does not attribute the difference" to "does not credit the software"
- Draft (H3): "The company's own note does not credit the software"
- Source: "the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software"
- Difference: the scope. The source concerns only the difference in median assignment time. The heading states that the note gives the software no credit at all.
- Concrete case: the note credits the log with making repair status visible across shifts but declines to attribute the assignment-time difference to it. The source is consistent with this, because it says nothing else about what the note concludes. The heading would then be false, while the source statement holds. No supplied statement excludes this case.
- Smallest repair: "The company's own note does not credit the software with the time difference". An alternative is "…does not attribute the difference to the software".

### F3 (minor). "During the eight-week trial" adds a time window to the count of 31
- Draft: "says 31 repair reports were entered during the eight-week trial"
- Source: "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial." "The trial lasted eight weeks."
- Difference: the time. The source gives the count without saying over what period it applies. It sets the trial's length separately and does not give its start date.
- Concrete case: the trial ran from early October to late November, and the note, dated 4 December, counts reports entered up to its date. That would include some entered after the trial ended. The source is consistent with this, and no supplied statement limits the 31 to the trial window. The draft's statement would then be false.
- Smallest repair: "says 31 repair reports were entered. The trial lasted eight weeks." A shorter option is to drop "during the eight-week trial" and state the eight weeks elsewhere, for example "…in the preceding eight-week period" already implies it.

## 3. Editorial question (not a defect)

- The source states: "The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism." The draft neither discloses this nor claims independence. It has a byline and keeps Svale in the third person throughout. Whether the piece needs a disclosure line is an editorial decision for the publisher and outside source support. The draft makes no false claim here.

## 4. Translation findings

None. The source and the draft are both in English, and no quotation was translated.

## Completion status

Complete. All claims, headings, the summary and the pronouns are accounted for. Three source-support findings remain unresolved: F1 (title), F2 (heading H3) and F3 (the time window on the count of 31, minor). There is one editorial question (the supplier-publication disclosure) and there are no translation findings.

# Source-support comparison: Elm Quay case draft

Draft: scratch/write-run.NkEBNV/draft.md
Source: work/source.md
Language: en_US. The source is English, so there are no translated quotations and no translation findings. Frontmatter is handoff metadata and makes no claims. The byline "By Thomas" comes from the invocation and is not a finding.

## Claim accounting

| # | Draft passage | Source passage | Difference / test | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Title: "Elm Quay tests one repair log across shifts" | "decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information." | Present-tense "tests" follows headline convention. The body says the trial has ended. "across shifts" matches the stated aim. | Supported |
| 2 | Dek: "A housing company's maintenance team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same repair information." | "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information." | "repair information" makes the repair-log context explicit. I found no case where the two statements diverge. | Supported |
| 3 | Dek: "how Elm Quay Housing ran an eight-week trial of software from Svale Systems" | "The trial lasted eight weeks."; "It chose Svale Systems"; "Svale configured the log"; "does not attribute the difference to the software" | Elm Quay stays the acting party, as the brief requires. | Supported |
| 4 | Dek: "what its own trial figures can and cannot show, and how its maintenance supervisor judges the result" | "Elm Quay's internal trial note"; "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"; "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." | "its" = Elm Quay: singular, non-personal. | Supported |
| 5 | "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 apartments" | "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats." | flats → apartments is the en_US term for the same thing. | Supported |
| 6 | "its telephone repair reports and emails used to be stored separately" | "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately." | "used to be" = "Previously". Both carry the same implied change, so the scope is unchanged. | Supported |
| 7 | "In September 2025 the company's own maintenance team decided to test a shared repair log in two buildings." | "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings." | Same. The date attaches to the decision, not to the start of the trial, as in the source. | Supported |
| 8 | "The eight-week trial has ended, and the team has yet to decide whether to expand it." | "The trial lasted eight weeks."; "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | "lasted" (past tense) and the dated note support "has ended". "has yet to decide" = "will decide". "it" = the trial. | Supported |
| 9 | H2: "Elm Quay tested the log before choosing Svale" | "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available." | The sequence is preserved. No supplier comparison is implied. | Supported |
| 10 | "Maya Lind, Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, answered questions about the trial by email." / "Lind wrote" | "Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"; "All interviews occurred by email" | Consistent with the email medium. The draft invents no scene or emotion. | Supported |
| 11 | Quotation 1: "We wanted the evening shift … put them into the log." | Quotation 1, source list item 1 | Verbatim. No repair was needed or made. | Supported |
| 12 | "the team tested whether the log could show the status of each repair" | "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair." | Same. | Supported |
| 13 | "Svale configured the log and trained six staff members in two sessions, while the team kept telephone reporting open for residents." | "The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions." | "while" makes the two actions concurrent, and keeping telephone reporting open plainly spans the setup. The customer remains the actor for categories through the adjacent quotation. | Supported |
| 14 | H2: "Expansion waits on how the categories hold up" | "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | See Finding 1. The source gives the timing of a decision. The heading turns it into a condition on expansion and drops "for larger repairs". | **Finding 1** |
| 15 | "Lind also wrote about the preparation:" + quotation 2 | Quotation 2 (verbatim); quotation 3 "I would leave an extra week for preparation" | The quotation is verbatim. Calling it "preparation" is a fair reading of "set that time aside before the next building starts". | Supported |
| 16 | "The team will decide whether to expand the trial after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | Same sentence in the source. | Same. | Supported |
| 17 | H2: "The note does not tie the faster assignment to the software" | "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period … the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." | The non-attribution is correct. "the faster assignment" drops the median and exclusion scope. See Finding 2. | **Finding 2** (minor) |
| 18 | "An internal trial note from Elm Quay, dated December 4, 2025, says 31 repair reports were entered. The note excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial." | "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial." | Same. The date is reformatted for en_US. | Supported |
| 19 | "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period." | Identical in the source. | Same. | Supported |
| 20 | "The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." | "The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." | Same. No causal claim appears anywhere in the draft. | Supported |
| 21 | "The figure covers time to assignment, not to completion. Completion time, cost and resident satisfaction were not measured." | "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements."; brief: "Do not turn assignment time into completion time." | "were not measured" matches the source's flat existential statement. The source uses "available" elsewhere ("No comparison … is available") but not here, so the draft's certainty matches the source's. | Supported |
| 22 | H2: "Lind weighs the trial as a whole" / "Lind's overall assessment is not drawn from those figures." | "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures." | "as a whole" and "overall" characterise a quotation that is about the trial itself ("do the trial again"). The source calls it her assessment without narrowing it to one aspect. The qualification survives inside the quotation and in the next sentence. The non-inference is carried exactly. This is defensible. | Supported |
| 23 | Quotation 3: "I would choose to do the trial again … extra week for preparation." | Quotation 3 | Verbatim. The hedge "but" and the conditional "would" are preserved. | Supported |
| 24 | "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company." | "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company." | Verbatim. The customer's reservation survives. | Supported |
| 25 | H2: "Other teams can begin with a checklist" | Brief: "The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist" | This is an author/publisher suggestion resting on the brief. | Supported |
| 26 | "Elm Quay has not yet made its decision on expansion." | "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after …" | Same. | Supported |
| 27 | "Operations managers weighing a similar trial can read the implementation checklist before setting aside their own preparation time. It is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial." | Brief: "it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial." | The link description matches the brief. "before setting aside their own preparation time" is the author's advice, echoing Lind's quotations. The draft does not attribute the checklist to anyone the source does not name. | Supported |

### Pronoun accounting (outside verbatim quotations)

- "its" (dek, twice; ¶1; H2 context; "its decision"): refers to Elm Quay Housing. Singular, non-personal. Supported.
- "it" ("expand it"): refers to the trial. Singular, non-personal. Supported.
- "their own preparation time": refers to operations managers. Plural. No gender is conveyed. Supported.
- "It is a document to read": refers to the checklist. Singular, non-personal. Supported.
- Lind: no third-person gendered pronoun is used anywhere, so the draft asserts no natural gender. Nothing to support.
- The first-person "we/us/I/ours" occurs only inside verbatim quotations and is the speaker's own.

### Quotations

All three quotations are reproduced verbatim from "complete usable quotations". There is no repair, welding or reordering. Each is correctly framed as written by email ("Lind wrote"). There is no translation, so there are no translation findings.

## Findings (source support)

### Finding 1: the heading turns decision timing into a condition and drops scope

- Draft (H2, line 22): "Expansion waits on how the categories hold up"
- Source: "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
- What differs: The source says only that the expansion decision will come after the check, and that the check concerns "larger repairs". The heading makes expansion the thing waiting, which presupposes it as the pending outcome. It also implies that how the categories perform is the condition for expansion. The heading also widens "work for larger repairs" to the categories in general ("hold up").
- A concrete case compatible with the material: the team checks the categories on larger repairs and they work well, but it decides against expansion for another reason (for example cost or staffing). Here the source holds (it decided after the check), but the heading fails (expansion did not follow the categories holding up). No supplied statement excludes this case.
- Smallest repair: "Expansion decision follows a check of the categories on larger repairs", or "The expansion decision waits on a category check".

### Finding 2 (minor): the heading generalizes a median comparison to "faster assignment"

- Draft (H2, line 28): "The note does not tie the faster assignment to the software"
- Source: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period." The note "excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial." The note "does not attribute the difference to the software."
- What differs: The source measures a median over the non-excluded reports. The heading asserts, without qualification, that assignment was faster.
- A concrete case compatible with the material: the median fell from three to two working days while a few long-delayed reports raised the mean, or while emergencies (excluded) were assigned more slowly. The source statement holds, but "faster assignment" as a general statement fails. No supplied statement excludes this case. The body gives the full qualification. The contract requires scope to be preserved in headings as well.
- Smallest repair: "The note does not tie the shorter median assignment time to the software", or "The note does not tie the difference to the software".

## Editorial question (not a source-support defect)

The source says the case is "supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism". The draft asserts nothing that contradicts this, and it claims no independence. Whether to disclose supplier publication in the text is a presentation choice outside this comparison. It is noted here only so the commissioning party can decide.

## Completion status

Complete. All factual and attributed claims, the headings, the dek, the quotations and the pronouns have been accounted for. Two findings remain unresolved: Finding 1 (H2 "Expansion waits on how the categories hold up") and Finding 2, minor (H2 "the faster assignment"). There are no translation findings.
